text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Moi says old-generation national identity cards will not be accepted during next general election.
- Parliament will extend session by two weeks to facilitate debate and enactment of laws which government promised World Bank it would have in place before end of year.
- Opposition Alliance backs churches in rejecting draft bill on regulation, registration, control of religious organisations.
- Leader of opposition Michael Kijana Wamalwa alleges plot to bar him from seeking presidency as chairman of FORD-Kenya.
- Health Minister Angatia says AIDS has killed over 200,000 Kenyans while 1.2 million are infected with deadly virus.
- Nairobi police recover two types of grenades and two pairs of police uniforms from house rented by one of four suspects arrested on Friday.
- Government has allowed imports of generators duty-free to alleviate power shortage.
- Roman Catholic priest from eastern province is for second time relieved of pastoral duties over allegations he engaged in sexual affair with local secondary school headmistress.
- Drive to make Dar es Salaam Stock Exchange a reality receives boost with announcement of trading and listing rules.
- Tripartite Commission of East African Co-operation will this week discuss revival of regional airline on lines of old East African Airways.

- Announcement by government that it will enforce 30-year-old law giving indigenous Kenyans exclusive rights to deal in certain products and areas of business has sent out conflicting signals about liberalisation of economy.
